rows.a: Consent: FY26/27 budget (Ord 2026-08), water/sewer rate increase (Ord 2026-09), sidewalk + Lions Park contracts, North Rd resurfacing IGA. Discussion: Block B rezoning & PUD.
rows.o: Consent passed 5-1 (Joseph no), adopting budget and rate increase. Block B PUD presented: 5 stories, 97 apts (62 1BR, 18 2BR, 17 studio), ~6,000 sf retail, 70 ft tall, 170 parking spaces (code calls for 185-215), rent ~$2.80/sf. P&Z had recommended 6-0; board directed approving ordinance unanimously. In trustee reports Joseph listed concerns from shadowing staff (HR, building inspectors, meeting materials, Fire Dept coordination). These remarks led to his censure on 5/5.
rows.p: Cimilluca: stormwater flooding on Ski Hill Rd. Seidel: Block B parking and facade. Hanahan: supports Block B, wants utilities buried.

rows.p: 50+ attended. Seidel read letter backing Joseph, said 3 FOIA requests unanswered, asked to move public comment later. Hughes asked for 7pm start. Meshes came for the censure, backed posting packets, worried about Block B parking. Psensky: fire equipment for 5 stories. Hameetman wanted to know who was censured, prefers 3 stories. Martin: Rec Council sign access, e-scooter safety.
rows.g: Trustee Joseph; Censure; Transparency; Block B; Grants

topics: Block B / Downtown TIF #3
Mixed-use redevelopment of the vacant downtown Block B lot (301/303 Opatrny, 300-316 Northwest Hwy) by FRG Partners (Harlem Irving + Hamilton Partners).

2024: Village demolished the Block B buildings: demolition bid to Omega III ($350K vs. $860K estimate) 3/19, demo April to June, site seeded by August. Knar pushed for developer incentives (2/6) and opposed other capital spending until Block B was under construction. 2025: 6/3 pre-application conference (Harlem Irving, Hamilton Partners, Zeller; 5 stories, 95 units, 7,000 sf retail); 6/17 resident John Martin called 5 stories too tall; 8/5 Teska hired to study a Block B-only downtown TIF (6-0); 11/11 board began planning long-term acquisition of Block C; 12/16 Res 2025-05 intent to use TIF. 2026: 1/20 TIF hearing; 2/17 TIF #3 created 6-0; 4/21 PUD presented (5 stories, 97 apts, 6,000 sf retail, 170 parking); 5/5 rezoning/PUD passed; 7/7 redevelopment agreement 5-1; 8/18 purchase & sale + first amendment 5-1. Joseph the lone no on the agreements. Residents raised parking, height, fire equipment.
Construction timing; parking; whether school districts' refusal to share TIF receipts costs the village.
Trustee Joseph censure & transparency
Trustee David Joseph pushed for changes (HR, building inspector conflicts, posting packets, recording meetings).

2025: Joseph sworn in 5/6/2025 (Schladt left the board); lone no on the 9/2 sales tax (wanted all offset fees cut to zero) and on 206 N River. 2026: 4/21 Joseph trustee report; 5/5 censured 5-1 (cited Open Meetings Act, quality governance, communication); 5/19 Seidel said the post in question was hers alone; 5/19 Hester asked about packets and recording; 6/16 board agreed to post expanded public packets (online starting 7/7). Recording still 'needs research'.
Video/audio recording of meetings; moving public comment later; 7pm start time; Joseph's HR and inspector questions.
Budget & water/sewer rates
FY 2026/27 budget and 4.75% water/sewer increase (~$4.04/mo average household).

2024: 3/21 workshop; 4/16 FY24/25 budget passed 4-1-1 (Schladt no, Knar present) and 3.6% water/sewer increase 6-0; 11/5 levy +4.30% passed 6-0; 11/12 board declined levy offsets. 2025: 3/12 workshop (3.4% proposed); 3/18 consensus on one-time $250,000 General Capital to Water/Sewer transfer with payback, base rate flat; 4/22 FY25/26 budget and 3% usage-rate increase passed 6-0; Kyle Platt repeatedly urged usage-based pricing; 11/4 levy +3.99% passed 4-2 (Knar, Migdal no). 2026: 3/11 workshop; 3/31 hearing; 4/21 adopted 5-1 (Joseph no); 5/5 budget amendment; 9/22 FY25/26 audit + fund transfers.
Whether base fee shifts to usage-based pricing.
Zoning cases
Variance and special-use requests.

2024: 906 Rte 22 adult day care (3/5, 6-0); 913 Rte 22 DA Racing car sales/repair (7/2, 5-0); Norge pole barn, 100 Ski Hill (8/6); 415 Ski Hill garage height denied 6-0 (8/20); 220 Gladys garage failed 8/6 with three trustees absent, then passed on reconsideration 9/3; shipping containers allowed in B3 by special use (8/6); accessory structure rules loosened (10/1). 2025: 912 NW Hwy massage school (3/4, 4-0); 418 Concord special uses rescinded after neighbor complaints (4/22, 6-0); 206 N River Rd (Allen) variances tabled 4/22, approved 6/3 4-2 plus President (Joseph, Knar no) over neighbor flooding concerns; Norge Ski Club container, 100 Ski Hill (6/3) and former Norge Park container (12/16); 107 Center porch (9/2) led to a covered-porch code change (11/4); business use table rewritten, cannabis dispensaries made a permitted use (6/3). 2026: 206 N River Rd (approved 2/17, 5-1); 408 Lincoln car sales lot (approved 6/16, 5-2); 601 Thackeray fence (approved 8/4); 502 NW Hwy pole sign (P&Z denied 3-1; board vote 9/22).
502 NW Hwy outcome.
Business grants (BCAP / facade)
Village grants to local businesses.

2024: The 100 Lounge BCAP $15,000 (1/16-2/6, Curtiss and Knar no) and facade $7,350 (8/20-9/3); 414 NW Hwy up to $50,000 considered (10/1); 412 Lincoln $16,000 agreed by consensus (12/17). 2025: Pence Holdings facade $16,000 (1/7, re-approved 9/2); Pieceful Gathering Quilt Shop $5,100 (1/21); Magical Forest Bookstore $12,000 (6/17-8/5; trustees split on $12K vs $15K); Lord of Beers $15,000 (8/19-9/2); All Marine facade up to $35,000 approved 10/21. 2026: All Marine facade $35,000 (2/3); All Ways Art Gallery $4,843 (2/17-3/3); Needle Drop Record Shop $15,000 (5/5-5/19).
Taxes & revenue swap (2025)
Board added a 1% grocery tax and 1% non-home rule sales tax, offset by cutting utility taxes to 1%.

2025: 8/5 grocery tax 6-0 (replacing state's repealed tax, ~$175K/yr); 8/19 sales tax directed 4-1 (Migdal no); 9/2 sales tax 5-1 (Joseph no) and telecom 6% to 1%; 9/16 cable 5% to 1%; 10/7 electricity 3% to 1%; 10/21 natural gas 5% to 1%. All effective 1/1/2026.
Whether new revenue and the cuts balance out; Platt and others want the grocery tax dropped.
401 Algonquin Rd demolition
Demolition of an abandoned building at 401 Algonquin Rd near Concord Ave.

2024: 11/5 village pursuing eminent domain and fencing the frontage; neighbors raised safety concerns. 2025: 6/17 Concord neighbors said they opposed the project from the start; 9/16 Fowler Enterprises low bid ($158,370) deadlocked 3-3 twice amid a fair-contracting group's complaints; 10/7 reconsidered and awarded 3-2 plus President (Knar, Wall no); 12/2 nearly demolished.
Cost recovery from the property (staff said steps will be taken); future use of the site.
1005 Rte 22 code enforcement
Business at 1005 Rte 22 repeatedly violated variance conditions (trucks and equipment parked outside, business outside the building).

2024: 2/20, 3/5 and 4/2 trustees flagged trailers parked day and night in the lot; owner ticketed. 2025: 4/3 Knar raised it, cure letter sent; 6/17 Ord 2025-16 rescinded the 2021 variations 6-0; 8/19 board unanimously refused a new variance (semis still parked); 11/4 judge ruled for the village, daily fines continue.
Tenant removal and compliance.
Parks & capital plan
Park upgrades, shoreline work and the 10-year Capital Improvement Plan.

2024: 4/16 Picnic Grove monument sign chosen, $35,181 contract 8/6; 6/18 park crowding, parking and grill complaints; 8/20 OSLAD application (boardwalk dropped); 12/17 $600,000 OSLAD grant awarded for Lions Park (~$1.9M project). 2025: 4/22 playground replacements at Hunters Farm and North River Park #2 (5-1, Knar no); 8/19 extra Lions Park shoreline work $29,900; 8/5 Hunters Farm natural area vandalized; 11/11 CIP: Lions Park master plan, Rte 14 right-of-way study, sidewalks near Lions Park, Picnic Grove deferred; 12/16 Lions Park equipment ordered.
Lions Park construction 2026; Picnic Grove improvements; Rte 14 corridor.
E-scooters & e-bikes
Village allowed low-speed e-scooters on local roads under state law; residents raised safety concerns.

2025: 5/6 board directed ordinance; 5/20 draft approved with 30 mph cap; 6/3 Ord 2025-14 passed 6-0; 6/17 John Martin asked for helmet rule; 8/5 residents raised e-bikes on sidewalks and near playgrounds.
Helmet or sidewalk rules.
Waste hauling contract
Residential garbage, recycling and yard waste contract.

2024: 5/7 RFP planned; 9/3 all three bids rejected as incomplete; 10/1 consensus to negotiate with LRS (vs. MDC, ~10% price gap); 11/5 LRS 5-year contract 2025-2030 approved 6-0 with free year-round yard waste and a second e-waste pickup.
Contract runs through 2030.
Parks & Special Events committees
Volunteer committees that run village events (Fox Fest, fireworks, tree lighting).

2024: 12/3 Special Events chair resigned; trustees discussed merging the committees and hiring a coordinator. 2025: 3/18 merger and contracted coordinator approved; 4/3 Ord 2025-06 combined them; 5/6 four firms interviewed.
How the contracted coordinator works out.
about: Fox River Grove Village Board tracker
A weekly Claude scheduled task checks the village site, adds new meetings here, fills in minutes once posted, and emails a summary.

Minutes are scanned images; they're read visually, so double-check exact wording against the PDF before quoting. Agendas usually post the Thursday before; minutes post ~2-5 weeks later after approval.
